newsitem.title: SENEGAL: French tourists killed in Senegal plane crash.
newsitem.headline: French tourists killed in Senegal plane crash.

text.p: A plane crash killed 20 people and injured 32 in Senegal on Saturday and France said most of the victims were probably French tourists.
The plane, chartered by Air Senegal, crashed shortly after take-off from Tambacouda in the centre of the West African nation, state radio said.
"After taking off the aircraft crashed on the tarmac and burst into flames," a witness told Dakar Radio.
The witness said the injured were thrown clear when the plane hit the runway.

"There are 20 people dead and 32 injured. Most of them are no doubt French people," French foreign ministry spokesman Yves Doutriaux said in Paris, adding the ministry had no exact number. He said that the passengers were mostly tourists.
"A plane of the Senegalese armed forces is taking the injured to Dakar to place them in the city's two hospitals," he said.
The French embassy in the former French colony had a list of passengers and was in touch with both the Senegalese authorities and the French foreign ministry.
The plane was due to fly to the former French colony's capital Dakar, 450 km (280 km) away.

Senegal is a favourite holiday destination for tourists from France and Germany -- particularly its separatist southern province of Casamance. African Americans on tours in search of their roots are also frequent visitors.

Two French couples disappeared while on holiday in Casamance in 1995. Despite extensive searches in and around the combat zone where troops and separatist rebels occasionally clash neither the tourists nor their bodies have been found.
The French foreign ministry has set up a crisis unit with a telephone for any worried relatives to call.
